steps.text: The man walks past rows of fallen bookshelves, trying to return the scattered books to where they should be.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: 'The Earth's blessings have granted this stone to its people; the Heaven's blessings shall bring an end to Sui'... but in this thousand-year river of history, is it fate ordained by heaven and earth, or nothing more than a coincidence?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Lord Zuo and Miss Ch'en...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It was they who brought the token to the Sky Mirror Pavilion today...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Was it a coincidence, or...
This mayhem... what happened?
Someone joins him, stepping lightly, and bends down to pick up a book from the ground.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning... why are you still here?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Did you forget that I am an official of the Ministry of Rites? Neither of us should leave, until all the civilians have been evacuated.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You are quite right...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Is the evacuation of the civilians complete?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Essentially. Baizao will soon separate.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Tis unsettling... is it not?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Perhaps you wanted to ask how I knew you were here, when you did not tell me about your demotion.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...It rained through the night yesterday. I only fear that you may be cold...
The man clears a little spot for the two of them to sit down.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: It has been a long time since I last visited the Sky Mirror Pavilion.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I suppose you used to frequent here?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: As did all the students of the Academy.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I had a headache whenever I looked up at the books stacked all the way up to the ceiling.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: But now... I find here a place of rare peace, away from the troubles beyond.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I... I heard about Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You have my deepest sympathies....

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: My grandfather did what he felt was right.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: He would not have kept the secret for so long out of selfish interests. He did it to protect the younger generations too.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I cannot reproach him, whether with reason or sentiment.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Of course, he must also pay the price for his deeds.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I see you have laid it down... I am glad to see it.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Perhaps you misunderstand. I do not mean that I could lay it down easily.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I cannot deny that my career benefited greatly from my grandfather's influence... those on the outside would undoubtedly say that the House of Ning has fallen on hard times.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I would not say this to anyone but you, Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You should not say that. I do not feel that any of your honors are undeserved.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I trust you—

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: What if you are the only one?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: My grandfather said that once one has passed the walls of the palace, one must not trust in others easily, and certainly not expect to be trusted easily.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I listened... but it seems that I forgot about it when I met you in Shangshu.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I simply believed that I found a kindred spirit.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You... you flatter me.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: You've always been like this.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I admire your honesty and your sense of responsibility, but I hate how you make decisions by yourself and keep other people at a distance.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: But then I realized... you would not be Liang Xun, if everything you did was to my liking.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I could no more reproach you than I could reproach my grandfather.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I once thought that all I needed to do was to be fair, honest, diligent, and persevering.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: But the years have taught me how powerless I am.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Your grandfather was right, but even more frightening is the thought that I could not even trust myself to keep my aspirations and ideals.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I would not claim that everything I did was honest and upright... but you should not have been involved in the ones that were not.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Is it my turn to comfort you with the words 'clear conscience'?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: You and I have done all we could, following the path of justice that we believed in.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Perhaps we are ultimately powerless to change anything. Perhaps this entire city will be no more when the sun rises tomorrow...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Then... here and now, at least... my conscience is clear.
The night is deep.
The ancient library has kept some old rules. All is quiet, except the passage of time.
They hold each other's hands tightly in their own.
The desolate pond lies wrinkled by the wind; beneath the crumbling eaves, no voices remain. One can still recall those days of green sashes and red plumes in their splendor...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The scriptgeists seem to be appearing less frequently.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Could it be that you were right, and these geists are the breathing of the bestial Sui...?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: I told you so. You just won't believe me.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Whatever the reason, this is our opportunity to head for the top—

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Hm... so this is the Sky Mirror Pavilion's restricted area.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What are you planning?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: These geists turn back into words when they're defeated.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Say, if they were transformed from the secret tomes of the Sky Mirror Pavilion, would defeating them reveal the secrets of Yan that are usually kept hidden?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You dare—?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: No sudden moves!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Let me see what secrets the words form!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: 'Sang' 'Tu' 'Cui' 'Shou'... what is this? It makes no sense.

spans.text: what is this? It makes no sense.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The top three floors of the Sky Mirror Pavilion are off-limits. We only enter because we have an important mission.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Refrain from doing anything unnecessary.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Hah. You still won't admit that you're already in on this.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Your deceptive words mean nothing. I know what I'm doing...

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: There's a lot that you don't know.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: This building began as a public library, one of the first buildings to be completed after Baizao became a nomadic city. But there was no such thing as a restricted area at the time.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Then, one hundred and twenty years ago, the death of the proxy affected tons of history books, causing their text to become unreadable.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: The Sui Regulator wanted to dig deep, but the number of books was enormous, so the Sky Mirror Pavilion set aside space up top for the Sui Regulator's research.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Decades passed. When the discussion of the turmoil had almost settled, the place became a warehouse for dusty old books.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Some restricted zone. Why would it be sealed off from public view, if it held any actual knowledge?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You do know a lot...

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Just a little bit more than you.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The things you speak of should not be secrets to the Sui Regulator. But I have not heard them before.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: My studies have been inadequate.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: You—this is what I hate about you. Always stiff, always by the book.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Was that white-haired Perro we met in Mangshan Town a friend of yours?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You mean... Yun Qingping?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Yeah, that's the name, I think.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: He couldn't fight his way out of a wet paper bag, and it looked like a stiff wind could blow him over, but he was a quick thinker. Talking to him was kind of interesting.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Why don't you learn a thing or two from him?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I know Yun's smart! I don't need you to lecture me!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Hahaha! Now you start to drop the official tone and sound like a human being.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...Why did you join the Shanhaizhong, Mo Yi?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: What answer do you want to hear?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: You want me to tell you that I had a difficult childhood, drifted into the Shanhaizhong, and I'm looking for a chance to repent and mend my ways?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Doesn't that sound a little cliche?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I wasn't—

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Say whatever you want.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Of course, the Shanhaizhong who murder and pillage are villains. They deserve to die.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: But I hate hypocrites even more, those people who look like they'll die if they stopped flaunting their high and mighty morals for a single moment.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: They think they're better than everyone else the moment they come out of their mama's tummy. Frauds!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What I really want to know is... why are you so sure that this thing from the Garden of Grotesqueries will stop a war between Yan and Sui?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: You've been with the Sui Regulator for a while. Have you never wondered about their most closely-guarded secret...?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Why did that proxy die?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Looks like it's not that you're not curious, it's that curiosity has yielded no answers.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: That's the problem, isn't it? Why would this have become a secret, if the Sui Regulator was really so just and upright?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: No, it's nothing...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Did you not hear any of that?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You're so weird. You've been staring into blank space for a while now.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Did those geists give you a concussion? Don't suppose there's anything I can do about that.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Thanks. I'm not quite—

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I just feel like...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I've been here before...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You said you've dreamt about this place before. Were you dreaming just now?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I thought I heard two people arguing... something about 'justice', but I'm not sure...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: You must be hearing things. It's mostly ancient history books here. Maybe there's a clue as to what's going on here, but justice? That's one thing you won't find.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: They seemed to be saying that justice doesn't exist, tangibly...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: That's true enough.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Never mind that. Let's get searching. Maybe you'll find your father's books here.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: His books, here?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Talk about forgetting one's roots.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: But I suppose it's not your fault. You didn't grow up in Baizao, and these things didn't really have anything to do with you.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I thought you would be angrier at me.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I am angry, but I realize I shouldn't take it out on you.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I just... never mind.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Miscellaneous Morsels from Baizao Suiyang... yes, this one dates back several generations.

spans.text: ... yes, this one dates back several generations.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: 'The people rejoiced as the new emperor took the throne. They put up white banners like clouds and held rites in remembrance of the previous emperor's virtue. But their hearts were hopeful, confident that an era of greatness was upon us, and the nation's peace secure...'

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: This is from a century ago, when the last True Lung took the throne.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: That's a long time ago. Does it have anything to do with what we're investigating?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The last True Lung's accomplishments were innumerable. The transformation of Baizao into a nomadic city, as well as the Sky Mirror Pavilion, were completed under his decree.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Not that either of us were around back then... although I suppose he would be your grandfather.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Look at this foreword... talk about sucking up to the powerful.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The county records from around Baizao and the demographic records of Baizao itself all paint a picture that is far less rosy.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: In the end, only one person's accomplishments remain.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Same old story no matter where you are, I guess.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: That is kind of strange to hear from a close blood relative of that emperor.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: 'When the city of Baizao was completed, the emperor ordered the tomes of all the archives to be gathered in a single place.'

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: 'The scholars worked by candlelight, collecting fragments and tales, validating the facts and compiling them, so that the scattered records are whole again.'

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: That's strange. The Imperial Historical Cabinet's efforts to collect the scattered histories happened after the death of the proxy, more than a decade before Baizao was built.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: But the ambiguous way that it's written... the older generations were always stringent about scholarship. Why would they make such a mistake?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Could it be that... even what little they left behind was altered and rewritten?
Ch'en Hui-chieh is not listening to her companion's muttering. She is on guard for any unusual movement around them.
She wanted to tell Ch'en Chao-ch'ien to get moving, but she had a hard time saying it, seeing the sad look on Ch'en Chao-ch'ien's face.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I never asked you... what happened to your family? The ones who were in Baizao?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The Ch'ens were a family of historians. They were well-regarded but not illustrious. They generally stayed out of conflict and politics, other than the occasional offense they inevitably caused in the course of their work as historians.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: All I remember is that my father said it was as though the sky had fallen when the family learned about the marriage arrangement with the princess.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: That cousin was the only unmarried man in the family. He, and everyone else, knew how dangerous it was, but they were in no position to refuse...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The rest was history. Princess Yanjing died in Lungmen, and my cousin passed away soon after.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: His Imperial Majesty did not punish our family, but rumors of strife took on a life of their own. You can imagine what happened to us when everyone decided our house had mistreated the princess.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: That's not what Mother wanted...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...I doubt it was Wei Yenwu's intention either.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I was very young then. All I saw was...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The elders were always sighing when they came back from the morning assembly. Many fell ill out of sheer worry. Brothers and sisters stopped communicating with one another...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Everything was shrouded in gloom, but I didn't know why.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Father moved from place to place, selling off the family's belongings, until we finally left Baizao altogether, yet he never once told me the reason.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: As for what happened after... you know, there was a time, after becoming Magistrate of Water here in the Sky Mirror Pavilion, when I thought I couldn't let the family tradition of history die with me.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I didn't complain about the job. Most of the position's responsibilities had been replaced by machines anyway; my colleagues, while not the friendliest lot, had little interest in political backstabbing.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I had time on my hands, so I thought I would start with my family's history.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Was it because the Magistrate of Water's rank was too low? I felt like I had stumbled into a thick fog, getting more lost with every step I took.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I knew my family didn't do anything wrong, but all the records I could find denounced us for our arrogance, our abuses.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I tracked down the ones who were still alive, tried to ask them what they knew. But they couldn't get away fast enough when they learned I'm of the Ch'en family, and the 'Chao' generation.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: The few who were willing to see me said a bunch of apologetic words in officialese, but refused to tell me anything about the truth of what happened...

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: I spent ten years on this until I even started to believe it myself, that the House of Ch'en deserved what it got for mistreating the princess!

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: But I know... I know it wasn't true!

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: What am I? What is the House of Ch'en? What were your dead parents?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: What is history?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: All I know is that history should be a record of the truth. That's what justice means to me.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Duoxie.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: As for the family history you wanted to know...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: To tell the truth... my parents died when I was very young. I don't remember much about them.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: And Wei Yenwu was... Wei Yenwu. It's hard for me to explain to people who my parents were. Sometimes I pass off the image of Wei Yenwu as my father's, just to make things simple.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I don't ever remember my mother smiling. And I don't remember many positive things about my father.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I just can't imagine how it feels... to have your life determined entirely by other people, by those baseless things like responsibility and honor.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: It's not fair to you... and it's not fair to them.

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Is life fair and just to anyone?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Someone once said to me that the justice we seek is not in the past... but that doesn't mean we should forget about it.
